episodes.label: The Signal That Tightened the Airway — SRS-A to Cysteinyl Leukotrienes, Zafirlukast Bound to Human CysLT1R (PDB 6RZ5), Inhaled LTD4 Bronchoprovocation vs. Chronic Asthma Trials & Idiosyncratic Hepatotoxicity
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 101: SRS-A to Cysteinyl Leukotrienes, Zafirlukast Bound to Human CysLT1R (PDB 6RZ5), Inhaled LTD4 Bronchoprovocation vs. Chronic Asthma Trials & Idiosyncratic Hepatotoxicity. A woman with asthma exhales 400 mL more in the first second after an inhaled bronchodilator. Weeks later, a different measurement changes the course of her care. The Critical Care Clinician follows airflow, symptoms and liver chemistry. The Molecular Pharmacologist follows a lipid signal from its synthesis to the airway receptor and the drug that occupies its pocket. The case, values and dialogue are fictional. Chapter 9, “The Eicosanoids: Cyclooxygenase, Lipoxygenase, and Epoxygenase Pathways” (2016), in the Pharmacology notebook introduces LTC₄, LTD₄ and LTE₄, their receptors and their effects on the airway. Primary studies establish the drug-specific evidence. Pharmacology notebook

episodes.label: The Channel That Opened Longer — CFTR G551D Open-Probability Defect, Ivacaftor (VX-770) Transmembrane Lasso/TM8 Hinge Binding (PDB 6O2P), STRIVE Sweat-Chloride vs. FEV1 Readouts & CFF Biomarker Interpretation
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 96: CFTR G551D Open-Probability Defect, Ivacaftor (VX-770) Transmembrane Lasso/TM8 Hinge Binding (PDB 6O2P), STRIVE Sweat-Chloride vs. FEV1 Readouts & CFF Biomarker Interpretation. Sweat chloride concentration falls to about half its pretreatment value. A spirometer shows a smaller change in a different unit. The patient, clinical values and host dialogue are fictional. The notebook anchor is H. Criss Hartzell’s 2010 Chapter 1, “Chloride Channels: An Historical Perspective,” especially section C on cystic fibrosis and CFTR agonists. The chapter predates U.S. ivacaftor approval. Pharmacology notebook · Hartzell, Chapter 1

episodes.label: The Blood Pressure Drug That Reached the Classroom — Guanfacine from Centrally Acting Antihypertensive to Prefrontal Alpha-2A HCN Regulation, Cryo-EM (PDB 7EJ8) & Pediatric ADHD/Tic RCTs
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 87: Guanfacine from Centrally Acting Antihypertensive to Prefrontal Alpha-2A HCN Regulation, Cryo-EM (PDB 7EJ8) & Pediatric ADHD/Tic RCTs. An 11-year-old wants to finish the first problem on a worksheet before losing their place. Their parent asks whether the same medicine might help the shoulder jerks and throat sounds that interrupt reading aloud. The Critical Care Clinician follows symptoms, daily function and circulation. The Molecular Pharmacologist traces an antihypertensive patent through receptor assays, primate recordings and trials with different clinical endpoints. The patient, observations and host dialogue are fictional. The notebook anchor is Andreas Hartmann’s 2013 chapter Clinical Pharmacology of Nondopaminergic Drugs in Tourette Syndrome, section 2.2 on guanfacine. Pharmacology notebook · Hartmann chapter

episodes.label: The Patch That Changed a Pain Fiber — Caterina's 1997 TRPV1 Cloning, Vanilloid Pocket Cryo-EM (PDB 7LPE), Reversible Epidermal Nerve-Fiber Defunctionalization (Kennedy) & 8% Capsaicin Patch Trials
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 85: Caterina's 1997 TRPV1 Cloning, Vanilloid Pocket Cryo-EM (PDB 7LPE), Reversible Epidermal Nerve-Fiber Defunctionalization (Kennedy) & 8% Capsaicin Patch Trials. A sock hurts a woman’s feet. A concentrated patch activates the channel that makes chili feel hot, yet her pain diary later records less burning. The patient, measurements and dialogue are fictional. The notebook anchor is Roman V. Frolov and Matti Weckström’s chapter “Harnessing the Flow of Excitation: TRP, Voltage-Gated Na⁺, and Voltage-Gated Ca²⁺ Channels in Contemporary Medicine,” published online December 10, 2015 and in the 2016 volume. Chapter record Pharmacology notebook

episodes.label: The Signal That Stopped the Migraine — Humphrey's 5-HT1B/1D Vascular Hypothesis, Subcutaneous Sumatriptan (US4816470 / US5037845), 5-HT1B Cryo-EM Comparator (PDB 6G79) & Human PET/MRA
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 83: Humphrey's 5-HT1B/1D Vascular Hypothesis, Subcutaneous Sumatriptan (US4816470 / US5037845), 5-HT1B Cryo-EM Comparator (PDB 6G79) & Human PET/MRA. A woman recognizes her usual migraine, but vomiting has made it difficult to keep fluids and tablets down. The Critical Care Clinician checks the time course, neurologic examination and vascular history. The Molecular Pharmacologist follows Glaxo’s GR43175 from vascular experiments and patent claims to human receptor pharmacology. The patient, observations and dialogue are fictional. The notebook source is Bockaert and colleagues’ 2010 chapter on serotonin receptor classification and signaling, specifically its discussion of 5-HT₁B, 5-HT₁D, 5-HT₁E and 5-HT₁F. Pharmacology notebook · Bockaert et al., receptor chapter

episodes.label: The Burn That Came Before Relief — TRPV1 Cloning (Caterina 1997), Reversible Epidermal PGP 9.5 Nerve-Fiber Defunctionalization & 8% Capsaicin Patch Neuropathic Pain Trials
episodes.notes: From nociceptor channel cloning to reversible peripheral nerve-ending remodeling: Caterina et al.'s (1997) expression cloning of the heat- and capsaicin-gated cation channel TRPV1, Kennedy et al.'s (2010) serial skin-punch biopsies quantifying ~80% reversible PGP 9.5 epidermal nerve-fiber loss and 24-week regeneration after a 60-minute 8% capsaicin patch, and contrasting Backonja (2008, low-dose active control in PHN) vs. Bischoff (2014, inert placebo in post-herniorrhaphy pain) RCT outcomes.

episodes.label: The Odor They Learned to Detect — Unilateral Nostril Androstenone Induction (Mainland 2002), Human OR7D4 Genetic Polymorphisms (Keller 2007) & Olfactory Training
episodes.notes: Peripheral vs. central plasticity in human olfaction: Mainland et al.'s (2002) single-nostril exposure experiment showing contralateral transfer of acquired androstenone sensitivity, Keller et al.'s (2007) and Lunde et al.'s (2012) OR7D4 RT/WM receptor variants governing odor intensity and valence in pork taint, and Gillmeister et al.'s (2025) olfactory perceptual training.

episodes.label: The Drug That Quieted the First Wave — Ondansetron & Cisplatin Emesis, 5-HT3A Cryo-EM (PDB 6W1M), Acute 5-HT3 vs. Delayed Substance P/NK1 Phase, hERG QTc Risk & CYP2D6 CPIC
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of ondansetron and biphasic chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting: Cubeddu & Marty's 1990 cisplatin trials, 2.8 Å cryo-EM structure of 5-HT3A bound to ondansetron (PDB 6W1M), why acute (0–24h) peripheral 5-HT3 vagal signaling gives way to delayed (24–120h) central NK1/Substance P signaling, hERG K+ channel blockade and FDA IV dose caps, and CPIC CYP2D6 ultrarapid metabolizer guidance.

episodes.label: The Venom That Took the Spinal Route — Intrathecal Ziconotide (ω-Conotoxin MVIIA), Olivera's Conus magus Discovery, Human CaV2.2 Cryo-EM Pore Plug (PDB 7MIX) & Slow Titration
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of intrathecal ziconotide (PRIALT / omega-conotoxin MVIIA): Olivera's discovery of Conus magus peptide toxins, Nieng Yan's 3.1 Å cryo-EM structure of human CaV2.2 plugged by ziconotide (PDB 7MIX), why systemic IV delivery causes orthostatic hypotension via sympathetic CaV2.2 block while intrathecal delivery targets dorsal horn lamina I/II synapses without tolerance or respiratory depression, and Staats (2004) vs. Rauck (2006) titration kinetics.

episodes.label: The Amino Acid at the Brain's Gate — Six-Competitor Plasma Tryptophan Ratio, Human LAT1 Cryo-EM (8J8M/8XPU), TPH2 & PET Tracer Assumptions, Delgado's Remission Relapse Trials (14/21; 8/15 vs. 1/15) & Breakfast Limits
episodes.notes: From plasma amino-acid competition at blood-brain barrier LAT1–CD98hc (PDB 8J8M L-Trp & 8XPU JPH203) to acute tryptophan depletion trials: UHPLC-MS/MS separation of isobaric Leu/Ile, recombinant TPH2 kinetics vs. alpha-[11C]methyl-L-Trp PET assumptions, Delgado's remitted depression crossover (14/21) and SSRI vs. desipramine responder split (8/15 vs. 1/15), and why Wurtman's breakfast study measured plasma ratios rather than mood.

episodes.label: The Gluten Fragment That Changed Its Charge — Celiac TG2 Cys277 Gln→Glu Deamidation, HLA-DQ2.5 Lysβ71 Pocket (1S9V), Irreversible ZED1227 Active-Site Trapping & Gluten-Challenge Biopsy Trials
episodes.notes: Atomic pathogenesis and covalent enzyme inhibition in celiac disease: tissue transglutaminase 2 (TG2) Cys277 thioester deamidation of gliadin glutamine into negatively charged glutamate, HLA-DQ2.5 positively charged P4/P6/P7 pocket anchoring via Lysβ71 (PDB 1S9V), tTG-IgA vs. total IgA and Marsh/villus-height-to-crypt-depth morphometry, and Schuppan et al.'s (2021) NEJM ZED1227 trial.

episodes.label: The Bowel That Learned to Absorb Again — Short-Bowel High-Output Jejunostomy Secretory Losses, GLP-2R Cryo-EM & Teduglutide Ala2→Gly2 DPP-4 Shielding & STEPS Parenteral Weaning
episodes.notes: Intestinal rehabilitation in short-bowel syndrome with end-jejunostomy: net secretory stoma sodium/water balance vs. renal sodium conservation, colonic salvage anatomy, human GLP-2–GLP-2R–Gs cryo-EM structure and teduglutide Ala2→Gly2 DPP-4 resistance, villus height/crypt depth trophic remodeling, and Jeppesen's STEPS randomized parenteral-support reduction trial.

episodes.label: The Calabar Bean & the Missing Signal — Physostigmine, Acetylcholinesterase Ser203 Carbamylation, Antimuscarinic Delirium & QRS Counterfactuals
episodes.notes: From Efik esere ordeal records in Old Calabar and Thomas Richard Fraser's Edinburgh experiments to human acetylcholinesterase Ser203 carbamylation (4EY4/1GQR), false-positive urine TCA immunoassays, and ECG QRS gating in antimuscarinic delirium.

episodes.label: How a Blood Vessel Tells Itself to Relax — Furchgott & Zawadzki's 1980 Intact vs. Rubbed Rabbit Aorta, Rubanyi's Donor-Detector Perfusion, Palmer & Moncada's Ozone Chemiluminescence Nitric Oxide Proof & 15N-Arginine Tracing
episodes.notes: How the vascular endothelium's relaxing signal was identified as nitric oxide: Furchgott & Zawadzki's (1980) discovery that removing the inner endothelial lining abolishes acetylcholine relaxation while preserving smooth-muscle contraction, Rubanyi et al.'s (1985) upstream donor/downstream denuded detector bioassay, Palmer, Ferrige & Moncada's (1987) chemiluminescent nitric oxide measurement alongside Ignarro's cGMP comparison, and 15N-arginine precursor tracing.

episodes.label: How Cells Tie Growth to Available Nutrients — Heitman & Hall's Yeast FPR1/TOR1/TOR2 Rapamycin Mutants, Sabatini & Brown's Mammalian mTOR Affinity Capture & Hara's Amino-Acid Withdrawal Gate
episodes.notes: Discovery of the TOR nutrient-sensing pathway: Heitman, Movva & Hall (1991) genetic screen in Saccharomyces cerevisiae showing rapamycin requires FKBP12 (FPR1) to inhibit TOR1/TOR2, Sabatini et al. (1994) & Brown et al. (1994) biochemical capture of the ~289 kDa mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) only when rapamycin is bound to FKBP12, Barbet et al. (1996) starvation-like translation arrest, and Hara et al. (1998) amino-acid gating of insulin-stimulated p70S6K phosphorylation.

episodes.label: How a Cell Passes a Message Inside — Sutherland & Rall's Broken-Cell Liver Homogenate Fractionation, Heat-Stable Cyclic AMP Transfer & Walsh's cAMP-Dependent Protein Kinase
episodes.notes: Discovery of the second-messenger principle: Rall, Sutherland & Berthet (1957) two-stage cell-free assay separating particulate membrane hormone response from soluble phosphorylase activation via a dialyzable, heat-stable factor, Sutherland & Rall (1958) chemical identification of cyclic 3',5'-AMP, and Walsh, Perkins & Krebs (1968) discovery of cAMP-dependent protein kinase (PKA).

episodes.label: The Mirror-Image Test for an Opioid Receptor — Goldstein's Stereospecificity, Pert & Snyder's [3H]Naloxone Levorphanol vs. Dextrorphan Assay & Enkephalin Discovery
episodes.notes: Biochemical proof of brain opioid receptors: Goldstein et al. (1971) enantiomeric competition concept, Pert & Snyder (1973) [3H]naloxone vacuum-filtration assay showing stereospecific displacement by (-)-levorphanol but not (+)-dextrorphan, Hughes et al. (1975) discovery of endogenous pentapeptides Met- and Leu-enkephalin, and 1992 delta-receptor cloning.

sections.heading: Everyday Patient Drug Safety, Pharmacogenomics & Maternal-Infant Risk

episodes.label: The Drug That Changed What HLA Shows — Abacavir F-Pocket Remodeling of HLA-B*57:01 Self-Peptide Repertoire (PDB 3VRI), PREDICT-1 Prospective Screening & Patch-Test-Confirmed vs. Clinical Hypersensitivity
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 94: Abacavir F-Pocket Remodeling of HLA-B*57:01 Self-Peptide Repertoire (PDB 3VRI), PREDICT-1 Prospective Screening & Patch-Test-Confirmed vs. Clinical Hypersensitivity. Nine days after switching to an abacavir-containing HIV regimen, a woman arrives with fever, rash and gastrointestinal symptoms. Her pretreatment genetic report was negative. The Critical Care Clinician asks what that result can establish once a patient is ill. The Molecular Pharmacologist follows abacavir into two different molecular systems, the viral polymerase and the human peptide-presenting complex. The case, measurements and dialogue are fictional. The notebook anchor is chapter 20, Adverse Drug Reactions, in the 2014 Handbook of Pharmacogenomics and Stratified Medicine, section 20.4.3.1 on abacavir hypersensitivity. Pharmacology notebook

episodes.label: The COX-2 Trade-Off — Inducible COX-2 Side-Pocket Sulfonamide Selectivity (PDB 3LN1 vs. 3KK6), Prostacyclin/Thromboxane & Renal Sodium Balance, APC/PRECISION/CONCERN Trials & Cardiorenal Monitoring
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 92: Inducible COX-2 Side-Pocket Sulfonamide Selectivity (PDB 3LN1 vs. 3KK6), Prostacyclin/Thromboxane & Renal Sodium Balance, APC/PRECISION/CONCERN Trials & Cardiorenal Monitoring. A woman who can finally climb her stairs notices that her shoes are tight. The Critical Care Clinician follows a change in kidney function while keeping her prior ulcer bleed and myocardial infarction in view. The Molecular Pharmacologist follows celecoxib from an inducible enzyme to a patent and a crystal structure. The patient, measurements and dialogue are fictional. Chapter 9 of the Pharmacology notebook, “The Eicosanoids: Cyclooxygenase, Lipoxygenase and Epoxygenase Pathways” (2016), introduces PGHS-2, celecoxib and the colorectal adenoma question. Pharmacology notebook

episodes.label: The Memory Drug and the Missing Beat — Donepezil Dual-Site Human AChE Gorge Spanning, Rogers & AD2000 Dementia Trials, Cholinergic Sinoatrial/AV Nodal Syncope & Prescribing-Cascade Pacemaker Risk
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 90: Donepezil Dual-Site Human AChE Gorge Spanning, Rogers & AD2000 Dementia Trials, Cholinergic Sinoatrial/AV Nodal Syncope & Prescribing-Cascade Pacemaker Risk. A woman taking donepezil briefly loses consciousness while seated. Later, while she is still on the monitor, the feeling returns. The Critical Care Clinician follows the atrial impulses that fail to reach her ventricles. The Molecular Pharmacologist follows Eisai’s inhibitor from the acetylcholinesterase gorge to the cognitive trials and the cardiac safety data. The patient, timings, bedside measurements and host dialogue are fictional. The notebook anchor is Brett A. English and Andrew A. Webster’s 2012 chapter 132, Acetylcholinesterase and its Inhibitors, which discusses donepezil’s reversible inhibition and Alzheimer indication. Pharmacology notebook · English and Webster chapter

episodes.label: The Drug That Kept GABA Outside — Tiagabine Off-Label Nonconvulsive Status Epilepticus, Human GAT1 Inward-Occluded Cryo-EM (PDB 7SK2 / 7Y7Z), Extrasynaptic Tonic GABAA & Salzburg EEG Criteria
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 86: Tiagabine Off-Label Nonconvulsive Status Epilepticus, Human GAT1 Inward-Occluded Cryo-EM (PDB 7SK2 / 7Y7Z), Extrasynaptic Tonic GABAA & Salzburg EEG Criteria. A woman with no known epilepsy stops answering questions halfway through a sentence. A new medication was meant to help her anxiety. The Critical Care Clinician follows her examination and video-EEG while the Molecular Pharmacologist tracks the GABA that remains outside neurons and astrocytes after GAT1 inhibition. The patient, measurements and dialogue are fictional. The notebook anchor, “Pharmacology and Biochemistry of Synaptic Transmission: Classical Transmitters,” is chapter 7 of the third edition of From Molecules to Networks (2014). It introduces high-affinity GABA uptake. The drug-specific evidence comes from the original studies and records linked below. Pharmacology notebook

episodes.label: The Glucose That Fell Again — Azole-Gliclazide CYP2C9 Interaction, SUR1/KATP Beta-Cell Closure, Recurrent Dextrose Rebound & Octreotide Suppression Trials
episodes.notes: Pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic feedback in recurrent sulfonylurea hypoglycemia: Gunaratne et al.'s (2018) nocturnal rebound drop from 106 to 25 mg/dL after voriconazole-to-fluconazole CYP2C9 inhibition with gliclazide, Aguilar-Bryan et al.'s (1995) cloning of beta-cell SUR1 gating KATP depolarization, Boyle et al.'s (1993) 8-volunteer crossover comparing dextrose alone, diazoxide, and octreotide, and Fasano et al.'s (2008) double-blind emergency-department octreotide RCT.

episodes.label: The Diuretic That Tried to Quiet Seizures — Neonatal Electrographic-Only Seizures, Developmental NKCC1/KCC2 Chloride Shift (Rivera/Dzhala), Bumetanide NKCC1 Cryo-EM (PDB 9C0H) & NEMO/Soul Trials
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 84: Neonatal Electrographic-Only Seizures, Developmental NKCC1/KCC2 Chloride Shift (Rivera/Dzhala), Bumetanide NKCC1 Cryo-EM (PDB 9C0H) & NEMO/Soul Trials. A newborn’s arm stops jerking. The scalp electrodes keep recording seizures. The Critical Care Clinician follows the discharges through cooling and rewarming. The Molecular Pharmacologist traces bumetanide from an edema patent to a chloride cotransporter. The case, measurements and dialogue are fictional. The notebook anchor is Criss Hartzell’s 2010 “Chloride Channels: An Historical Perspective.” Pharmacology notebook · Hartzell chapter

episodes.label: The Rhythm That Changed Its Shape — Flecainide 1:1 Atrial Flutter & Use-Dependent QRS Widening, Cardiac Nav1.5 Pore Block (Jiang 2020) & The CAST Surrogate-Endpoint Paradox
episodes.notes: Ion-channel kinetics and clinical trial epistemology in Class IC antiarrhythmic therapy: Dardas et al.'s (2021/2022) flecainide atrial flutter 1:1 AV conduction with wide-complex tachycardia, Jiang et al.'s (2020 Cell) cryo-EM structure of cardiac Nav1.5 central-cavity flecainide binding, Ranger et al.'s (1989) exercise-amplified use-dependent QRS prolongation from slow unbinding, and the 1989 CAST mortality reversal.

episodes.label: The Drug That Redirected Another — Azathioprine + Allopurinol Xanthine-Oxidase Blockade, 6-TGN Pancytopenia vs. 6-MMP Hepatotoxicity & Deliberate Low-Dose Co-Therapy
episodes.notes: Metabolic pathway redirection in thiopurine pharmacology: Feinman et al.'s (2020) heart-transplant pancytopenia after unadjusted allopurinol addition blocked xanthine oxidase and flooded 6-thioguanine nucleotides (6-TGN), Blaker et al.'s (2013) thioxanthine-mediated TPMT inhibition in red cells, Aizawa et al.'s (2025) metabolite profiling, and Kiszka-Kanowitz et al.'s (2022) randomized trial harnessing low-dose thiopurine + allopurinol in ulcerative colitis.

episodes.label: When Maltose Read as Glucose — Icodextrin Peritoneal Dialysis Metabolites, GDH-PQQ Test-Strip Cross-Reactivity vs. Core-Lab Hexokinase & Occult Neuroglycopenia
episodes.notes: Drug-assay cross-reactivity between peritoneal dialysis polymers and bedside point-of-care glucometers: Riley et al.'s (2003) icodextrin case where systemic alpha-amylase generated maltose/maltotriose that read as severe hyperglycemia on GDH-PQQ strips while true laboratory hexokinase glucose was critically low, Olszowska et al.'s (2019) metabolite kinetics, Cho et al.'s (2016) strip-enzyme interference bench testing, and Frias et al.'s (2010) FDA adverse-event series.

episodes.label: The Signal the Poison Interrupted — Delayed Belladonna Atropine Rebound via LC-MS/MS, Scopolamine Hippocampal Theta Disruption & Physostigmine vs. Lorazepam in Antimuscarinic Delirium
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology investigation of central and peripheral muscarinic blockade: delayed gastrointestinal absorption and day-4 LC-MS/MS serum atropine rebound after belladonna ingestion (Hayashi et al. 2026), human intracranial EEG evidence of scopolamine disrupting hippocampal theta oscillations during memory encoding (Gedankien et al. 2023), and randomized trial evidence comparing physostigmine cholinesterase inhibition against lorazepam sedation in antimuscarinic delirium.

episodes.label: The Pump at the Brain — Blood-Brain Barrier P-Glycoprotein (ABCB1) Efflux, Loperamide vs. Fentanyl CNS Exclusion, Cryo-EM ATPase Cycle & Drug-Drug Interactions
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology deep dive into blood-brain barrier ABCB1 (P-glycoprotein) efflux: why potent mu-opioid agonists like loperamide act peripherally unless P-gp is overwhelmed or inhibited, inward-to-outward cryo-EM peristaltic extrusion, and clinical transporter inhibition.

episodes.label: The Muscle That Waited — Prolonged Post-Succinylcholine Neuromuscular Blockade, Zero Train-of-Four Twitches, Dibucaine Number 41 vs. Catalytic BChE Activity & BCHE Genotyping
episodes.notes: Pharmacogenetics and clinical management of prolonged succinylcholine apnea (Hubbell et al. 2025): why a short-acting depolarizing neuromuscular blocker lasted 8 hours after hip surgery, peripheral nerve stimulator absence of twitches, distinguishing quantitative butyrylcholinesterase deficiency from qualitative atypical variants via the dibucaine inhibition number, and BCHE sequencing.

episodes.label: The Letter the First Test Missed — Compound Heterozygous DPYD Variants Missed by 4-SNP Panels (de Haar-Holleman 2024), Fluorouracil Catabolism Collapse & Uridine Triacetate Antidote Rescue
episodes.notes: Pharmacogenomics and biochemical rescue of fluoropyrimidine toxicity: why targeted 4-variant DPYD genotyping misses rare in-trans compound heterozygotes (de Haar-Holleman et al. 2024), phenotypic DPD uracil breath/plasma assays (Coenen et al. 2019), 5-FU catabolic shunting into FUTP/FdUMP (Peters et al. 1988), and emergency antidote rescue with uridine triacetate (Jacob et al. 2022).

episodes.label: The Drug That Cut the Drug — Glucarpidase Methotrexate Rescue, DAMPA Immunoassay Cross-Reactivity vs. HPLC/LC-MS/MS (5.79 vs. 2.27 µmol/L at Hour 117, Gulley 2020), Ogawa Tissue Rebound & Organ Recovery
episodes.notes: Enzymatic drug cleavage and analytical cross-reactivity after high-dose methotrexate rescue with glucarpidase (carboxypeptidase G2): Gulley et al.'s (2020) split specimen 74 hours post-glucarpidase reading 5.79 µmol/L by immunoassay vs. 2.27 µmol/L by HPLC due to DAMPA metabolite persistence beyond the nominal 48-hour VORAXAZE label window, Ogawa et al.'s (2024) 98.83% 20-minute plasma drop and tissue rebound, and Corbisier et al.'s (2024) multimodal pediatric liver/renal recovery.

episodes.label: The Blood That Would Not Turn Red — Acquired Methemoglobinemia (SpO2 86% vs. PaO2 85 mmHg), Multi-Wavelength Co-Oximetry, NADPH Reductase & G6PD Methylene Blue Hemolysis
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology deep dive into acquired methemoglobinemia and antidote mechanics: why dual-wavelength pulse oximetry locks near 85–86% despite high dissolved arterial PaO2, multi-wavelength co-oximetry separation of ferric (Fe3+) methemoglobin, how methylene blue uses NADPH methemoglobin reductase as an artificial electron shuttle, and why G6PD deficiency converts methylene blue into a trigger for acute Heinz-body hemolysis (Mathiyalagan et al. 2025; ProvayBlue US label).

episodes.label: The Number the Antidote Raised — Digoxin Immune Fab Redistribution vs. Immunoassay Interference, Ultrafiltration Free Digoxin (Jortani 1999), Renal Rebound Kinetics (Ujhelyi 1993) & Chronic Cardiogenic Shock
episodes.notes: Separating true pharmacokinetic tissue redistribution from platform-dependent immunoassay interference after digoxin immune Fab: Smith et al. (1976) 12-fold total serum rise with undetectable free digoxin, Jortani et al. (1999) ultrafiltrate immunoassay bias across platforms, Ujhelyi et al. (1993) delayed free-digoxin rebound in renal dysfunction, and Gerritsma et al. (2025) chronic digoxin cardiogenic shock.

episodes.label: The Antibiotic at the Other Ribosome — Linezolid Hyperlactatemia, Mitoribosome COX-II vs. Nuclear Tom20/SDHA Translation, Paired PBMC Recovery & Duration Cohort Denominators
episodes.notes: Translational pharmacology and mitochondrial toxicology of oxazolidinone antibiotics: linezolid-associated hyperlactatemia despite 98% arterial oxygen saturation (Chaudhri et al. 2024, 4.9->5.1->1.6 mmol/L), selective depletion of mitoribosome-encoded cytochrome c oxidase subunits vs. nuclear-encoded Tom20 and SDHA in human HL-60/THP-1 cells (Milosevic et al. 2018), paired patient PBMC recovery (Garrabou et al. 2007, COX-II protein 16% and enzyme activity 51% of controls with intact mtDNA/mRNA), and 40-patient cross-sectional duration cohorts (Martínez-Guitián et al. 2026).

episodes.label: The Drug That Changed With the Fever — Clozapine 1975 Finland Cluster & Kane 1988 Trial, Human H4–Gi Structure (PDB 8JXV), CYP1A2 Inflammation/Smoking Shift & AGP Binding
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 82: from the 1975 Finnish agranulocytosis cluster (Idänpään-Heikkilä et al.) and Kane et al.'s (1988) treatment-resistant schizophrenia trial (38/126 vs. 5/141) to ancillary human H4-Gi cryo-EM structure (PDB 8JXV), why acute pneumonia and abrupt smoking cessation elevate serum clozapine and the clozapine:norclozapine ratio via IL-6 CYP1A2 suppression and de-induction (Faber & Fuhr; Dickmann; Raaska), alpha-1-acid glycoprotein (AGP) unbound-fraction buffering, and the June 2025 FDA clozapine REMS removal.

episodes.label: The Channel That Quieted Insulin — Congenital Hyperinsulinism Critical Samples, Diazoxide KATP Opening, SUR1/Kir6.2 Comparator (PDB 7W4O), KCNJ11 Genetics & Pulmonary Hypertension
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 81: neonatal hypoketotic hypoglycemia critical-sample diagnostics (simultaneous glucose, insulin, C-peptide, beta-hydroxybutyrate, and free fatty acids; Ferrara et al.), repurposing antihypertensive benzothiadiazine diazoxide (Drash & Wolff 1964), beta-cell SUR1/Kir6.2 KATP opening and NN414 comparator structure (PDB 7W4O), dominant KCNJ11 p.Phe55Leu gating vs. recessive focal 11p15 loss, and echocardiographic surveillance for diazoxide-associated pulmonary hypertension (Herrera et al., 7/295).

episodes.label: The Drug That Emptied the Vesicle — Rauwolfia & Reserpine Discovery, Human VMAT2 Cytoplasm-Facing Complex (PDB 8JTC), Orthostatic ΔHR/ΔSBP & Prolonged Monoamine Depletion
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 80: from Vakil's (1949) Rauwolfia root reports and Müller, Schlittler & Bein's (1952) reserpine isolation to V-ATPase 2H+:1 amine stoichiometry (Knoth et al.), human VMAT2-reserpine cytoplasm-facing cryo-EM coordinates (Wu et al. PDB 8JTC, Tyr341/Tyr433; Pidathala et al. PDB 8T6A), why noncovalent transporter blockade produces prolonged vesicular monoamine depletion and blunted orthostatic heart-rate compensation, and bounded interpretation of Freis's (1954) depression case series.

episodes.label: The Walk That Became a Seizure — Dalfampridine (4-AP) in Demyelinated Axons, Kv1.2/Kv2.1 Architecture (PDB 2R9R), Timed-Walk Trial Denominators & Renal Seizure Risk
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 77: dalfampridine (4-aminopyridine) conduction rescue in diphtheria-toxin demyelinated rat spinal roots (Bostock, Sherratt & Sears 1978–1981), Kv1.2/Kv2.1 paddle-chimera selectivity filter coordinates (PDB 2R9R, Val371/Gly372), Goodman et al. episodes.label: The Antibody and the Unhealed Colon — Infliximab TNF-Alpha Trimer Crystal Structure (PDB 4G3Y), Transmembrane Avidity, Endoscopic Mucosal Healing (ACT 1/2) & Anti-Drug Antibody Clearance
episodes.notes: Structural immunology and therapeutic drug monitoring of infliximab in ulcerative colitis: chimeric cA2 engineering (Knight 1993), 2.60 Å TNF-alpha:infliximab Fab crystal structure (PDB 4G3Y, Liang 2013), transmembrane TNF bivalent avidity (Scallon 2002), ACT 1 & ACT 2 mucosal healing trials (Rutgeerts 2005), and anti-drug antibody clearance vs. assay non-interchangeability.

episodes.label: The Drug That Took the Long Way — Parkinson's Vallecular Tablet Retention on Videofluoroscopy, Enterococcus faecalis TyrDC Gut Decarboxylation & Oral vs. Jejunal Levodopa-Carbidopa Gel Kinetics
episodes.notes: Mechanical and microbial bottlenecks along levodopa's route from mouth to brain: videofluoroscopic discovery of tablet retention in the valleculae (Sato et al. 2018), carbidopa-insensitive gut microbial tyrosine decarboxylase (Enterococcus faecalis TyrDC) and Eggerthella lenta dopamine dehydroxylase (Maini Rekdal et al. 2019; van Kessel et al. 2019), and oral vs. continuous jejunal infusion pharmacokinetics (Othman et al. 2015).

episodes.notes: Intraoperative malignant hyperthermia from capnography to channel biophysics: why rising end-tidal carbon dioxide precedes core temperature elevation, uncontrolled skeletal muscle ryanodine receptor (RyR1) sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium release, dantrolene sodium stabilization of RyR1, and post-crisis workup integrating RYR1 variant sequencing with caffeine-halothane contracture testing.

episodes.notes: From Albrecht Fleckenstein's discovery of calcium antagonism to critical-care toxicology: rabbit CaV1.1 cryo-EM structure bound to (S)-verapamil in two central-cavity poses (PDB 6JPA), AV-nodal conduction block, pancreatic beta-cell L-type channel blockade producing diagnostic hyperglycemia, stereoselective CYP3A4 clearance, high-dose insulin euglycemia therapy, and EXTRIP non-dialyzability.

episodes.label: The Sedative the Screen Missed — GABAA alpha1-beta2-gamma2 Cryo-EM Allosteric Binding (6X3X/6X3U), Diazepam CYP2C19/3A4 vs. Lorazepam Direct UGT2B15 Glucuronidation & Why Urine Immunoassays Miss Lorazepam-Glucuronide
episodes.notes: Receptor allostery, metabolic routing, and toxicology screen blind spots: cryo-EM structures of human alpha1-beta2-gamma2 GABAA receptors bound to diazepam (PDB 6X3X) and flumazenil (PDB 6X3U), Sternbach's benzodiazepine chemistry, diazepam CYP oxidation vs. lorazepam direct C3-OH glucuronidation, and why unhydrolyzed urine benzodiazepine immunoassays miss lorazepam-glucuronide without beta-glucuronidase hydrolysis and LC-MS/MS.

episodes.label: The Dose That Bought Another Hour — Parkinson's Levodopa Wearing-Off Diaries, Catechol-O-Methyltransferase (COMT) Mg2+ Coordination (PDB 7XGI), Opicapone Erythrocyte Kinetics, BIPARK-I & Tolcapone Hepatotoxicity
episodes.notes: From Parkinson's wearing-off diaries to peripheral COMT inhibition: separating seated motor OFF time from orthostatic hypotension, competing AADC and COMT metabolic pathways, rat soluble COMT crystal structure bound to opicapone and Mg2+ (PDB 7XGI), plasma LC-MS/MS vs. sustained erythrocyte COMT inhibition kinetics, BIPARK-I/II trial endpoints, and tolcapone vs. opicapone hepatic safety.
